headline: US and Israel finalize 12 Apache helicopter deal amid escalating Middle East tensions
subheadline: Israel transfers one billion shekels to its Defense Ministry to approve the purchase of 12 AH-64E Apache helicopters for delivery in the 2030s.
lede: Israel and the United States sealed a deal for 12 AH-64E Apache helicopters, with deliveries slated for the 2030s after a billion‑shekel transfer to the Israeli Defense Ministry. Meanwhile, the Israeli military launched a commendation process for October 7 heroism, reviewing recommendations at field and corps levels. In Ukraine, Russia’s overnight barrage crippled railway infrastructure across five regions, while Geran‑5 rockets killed six and injured twelve in western cities. Ukrainian forces retaliated by destroying a Mi‑28 helicopter, striking the Borisoglebsk airbase and a Sberbank data center, and liberating 101 km² near Kharkiv.

sections.title: Russian strikes cripple Ukrainian railways, Ukrainian counterattacks continue
sections.body: Russian drones and missiles targeted railway depots, repair plants, and stations in Kharkiv, Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Khmelnytskyi, and Ternopil overnight. Geran‑5 rockets struck Rivne and Lutsk, raising the death toll to six and injuring twelve, including a child. SpaceX abruptly limited Starlink StarShield terminals to 100 mph, disrupting Ukrainian command and ISR operations. Ukrainian forces destroyed a modernized Mi‑28 helicopter with an FPV drone, attacked the Borisoglebsk airbase and a Sberbank data center in Saratov, and liberated 101 km² near Kharkiv.

sections.title: US‑Israel defense ties deepen with Apache deal, naval and humanitarian incidents
sections.body: Israel and the United States finalized a contract for 12 AH‑64E Apache helicopters, deliveries beginning in the 2030s after a billion‑shekel transfer to the Defense Ministry. The Israeli military opened a commendation process for acts of heroism during the October 7 battles, with recommendations reviewed at field and corps levels. A U.S. Navy F‑35C from VX‑23 achieved its first arrested landing and catapult launch aboard a Ford‑class carrier, operating from the future USS John F. Kennedy. U.S. forces eliminated an Iranian‑affiliated dhow surveilling American ships in the Gulf of Oman, evacuating the crew prior to the strike.

sections.title: Intelligence Assessment
sections.body: The Apache deal and joint carrier operations illustrate deepening U.S.‑Israeli defense integration amid heightened Iranian proxy activity, including dhow surveillance and Houthi missile manufacturing. Meanwhile, Russia’s concentrated railway strikes and Ukraine’s asymmetric attacks on rear‑area airbases and data centers signal an escalation toward broader logistical and economic warfare.
